key_insight: PrePR-CT uses inductive biological priors—explicitly integrating network knowledge—so ML models can accurately and interpretably predict cell‑type‑specific drug responses even with very limited labeled data.
problem_solved: How to predict drug responses for specific cell types when experimental labels are scarce, avoiding overfitting while providing mechanistic interpretability useful in early drug discovery.
method: Embed graph-structured biological knowledge as inductive priors to bias model learning toward biologically plausible relationships.
Train models in the small-data regime by sharing information across cell types and drugs via the prior, improving sample efficiency and generalization.
Produce interpretable predictions by linking model outputs to network components/pathways (enabling attribution of predicted responses to biological modules).
impact: Demonstrates a practical blueprint for combining domain priors with ML to get reliable, interpretable predictions from limited biological data—useful for practitioners building robust models in resource-constrained experimental settings.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: inputs (drug chemical + cell type + biological network) → PrePR-CT model → cell‑type‑specific response predictions.
Network overlay: biological network nodes/pathways highlighted to show how inductive priors guide model inference and attribution.
Comparison chart: small‑data performance (PrePR-CT vs baseline) showing improved accuracy and calibration with few labels.
Interpretability panel: heatmap or bar chart linking predicted responses to top-ranked pathways/genes for a given drug–cell pair.
paper_title: Predicting and interpreting cell-type-specific drug responses in the small-data regime using inductive priors
paper_authors: Reem Alsulami, Robert Lehmann, Sumeer A. Khan, Vincenzo Lagani, Alberto Maillo
